application.quote: Patients will be allowed to request financial assistance up to 240 days from the date of the patient's first statement, or any time during the collection process.

notes: The policy states that patients will receive their first statement within 45 days of discharge from the facility.
The policy mentions that DMH contracts with Trubridge and Mid-South Adjustment Company, Inc. for patient and/or guarantor collection processes.

The policy states that if during the course of collections follow-up, a patient or guarantor requests financial assistance or indicates that they are uninsured and cannot pay for their care, they will be referred to DMH's financial assistance team to be screened for potential financial assistance eligibility.

The policy states that once the application is received, regardless of completeness, all further collection activity will be stopped pending a decision from the financial assistance team on assistance eligibility.
The policy states that approved applications are valid for the visit(s) in which they are applying and for three months following the approved application.
The policy states that patients should allow 7 business days for the review process.
The policy states that the Financial Assistance decision will be valid and useable for the accounts listed at the time of application and for three (3) months after approval.

The policy states that it is preferred, but not required, that a request for Financial Assistance and a determination of financial need happens before any pre-scheduled non-emergency medically necessary services.

The policy states that if a patient cannot make a substantial payment or commit to a payment plan to resolve their approved discounted medical bill, all elective and non-urgent hospital procedures and related services may be deferred.
The policy states that falsification of information, lying, or incomplete documentation from the patient or responsible party could result in a denial of Financial Assistance.

The policy states that having said all of the above, the amounts charged for emergency and necessary medical services to patients who are eligible for Financial Assistance under this Policy will not be more than the amount generally billed to individuals with insurance covering the same care.

The policy lists reasons for denial including sufficient income, sufficient asset levels, patient uncooperative or unresponsive, requests for care when there is no identifiable means of obtaining long-term support, incomplete application despite reasonable efforts, pending insurance or liability claim, withholding insurance payment and/or insurance settlement funds.
The policy states that notices will be posted in key areas, including Admissions and Emergency Department advising patients that DMH provides financial assistance.
The policy states that current and complete copies of the Financial Assistance Policy and application form will be available on DMH's website along with a plain language summary of the policy.
The policy states that plain language summary copies of this policy will be distributed to the local DHS office.
The policy states that written information regarding this Financial Assistance Policy will be provided to all patients who request the information, whether at admission or any other time.

The policy states that DMH will ensure that front-line staff are able to answer questions regarding this Financial Assistance Policy effectively or direct such inquiries to the appropriate department.
